title: Zhang Fei Drinks His Way Through Zhang He; Huang Zhong Takes Mount Tiandang
summary: Zhang Fei, facing an opponent who will not come down off a mountain, camps in front of him and drinks for fifty days in plain view, until Zhang He comes down to take advantage of a drunkard — and finds that the man at the table is a straw figure.
Huang Zhong, now over sixty and tired of being called old, takes Mount Tiandang and its granaries by letting himself be underestimated for a fortnight.
history: Both are historical victories; the staged drunkenness is the novel's, and it is exactly the sort of joke Zhang Fei's reputation invites.
